title: The Copper Typewriter
premise: In 1913, Tamsin Eriksen serves as driver and confidant to suffragist leader Maren Eriksen, reading and sometimes quietly destroying letters to protect the family's secrets — including the truth about a death Maren's brother caused years ago. When the seasonal bridge closes, stranding the household with a wounded union organizer hiding from the constable, Tamsin must decide whether to keep the old silence that protects Maren or break it to save an innocent man. The last berth on the winter mail boat becomes the story's fulcrum: Tamsin gives it to the organizer, testifies with the copper typewriter's hidden letters as evidence, and chooses truth over loyalty — ending the novel with Maren, stripped of power but freed of guilt, asking Tamsin to drive her one last time.
about_author: Casper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing private correspondence in northern coastal towns. They write historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet Tamsin steaming open letters in the Eriksen house's back room, establishing their role as keeper of silences and the copper typewriter that produced the family's most dangerous documents twenty years ago. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into unease as a new letter arrives bearing an old, familiar seal.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The last cart crosses before the bridge shuts for the season; among those stranded is Ilse Brandt, a wounded union organizer the constable wants. Maren orders her hidden. Emotional beat: dread — Tamsin recognizes that sheltering Ilse will force every buried secret into the open.

chapters.title: What the Brother Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin and Maren POVs via letters. Flashback threads reveal that Maren's brother Anders caused a mill death in 1893, covered up by letters typed on the copper machine. Emotional beat: Maren's guilt surfacing as she reads Tamsin's face and realizes what they know.

chapters.title: A Constable at the Gate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The constable arrives searching for Ilse; Tamsin lies smoothly for the first time against their own instincts, buying time but binding themselves deeper. Emotional beat: the thrill and shame of complicity — invisibility has become a cage.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. News comes: one berth on the winter mail boat, one passenger only. Maren drafts a list — herself (the movement needs her), Ilse (the law wants her), or young cousin Petra (pregnant, fragile). Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of love, each option a betrayal.

chapters.title: Ilse's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Recovering, Ilse tells Tamsin she witnessed the 1893 cover-up as a child and has spent years gathering proof — proof that names Anders and implicates Maren's silence. Emotional beat: Tamsin's loyalty fractures; protecting Maren now means protecting a lie.

chapters.title: The Copper Machine Speaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin retrieves the hidden letters from the typewriter's false drawer and confronts Maren privately. Maren confesses she knew and stayed silent to preserve the movement. Emotional beat: grief — two people who loved each other through paper discovering the cost of their protection.

chapters.title: Which Silence Keeps People Safe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The constable returns with a warrant; Anders, drunk and desperate, tries to burn the letters. Tamsin saves them from the fire and decides: the berth goes to Ilse, whose testimony can free the wrongly accused mill foreman still imprisoned. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At the dock, Maren hands Ilse the berth and the letters, publicly breaking with her brother and accepting arrest alongside him. Tamsin drives them both to the courthouse. Emotional beat: catharsis — loyalty transformed, not abandoned; justice chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Letters Worth Reading
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, spring. The bridge reopens; the foreman walks free, Anders faces trial, and Maren, diminished but unburdened, asks Tamsin to read her letters aloud now — no more steaming, no more secrets. Emotional beat: quiet hope; inheritance redefined as truth passed openly between generations.
